findings.description: SHEET-MARK-005's second clause — "while offline, the kernels shall use the last cached marks with their quote-epoch stamps" — has no implementation or test in the sheets-view code under audit. The real `read_marks` (lib.rs L817-887), on a transport failure, does exactly one thing: propagate `Err` from `client.read_price_pass()?` and return with NO `MarksProduced` — it never reads or returns `prior`. The only place cached-mark substitution is described is a doc comment (L806-816) that attributes it to a *different*, unaudited crate: "The offline carry-forward is runtime's: on Err, runtime retains its existing cached marks... and re-injects them into the next replay." The one test covering this path, `transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks` (tests/marks.rs L131-159), asserts only `result.is_err()` — it does not (and cannot, from this crate) verify that cached marks with quote-epoch stamps actually get used anywhere. All three A-direction sketches, working from the EARS text alone, treat this as an in-scope, directly-implementable requirement and build a first-class offline-resolution mechanism for it: A1's `MarkCache::resolve()` gated by `is_offline()`, A2's `resolve_offline()`, A3's `Connectivity::Offline => self.0.get(&symbol)...` branch. All three B-direction reconstructions, working from the code alone, converge on the opposite conclusion — the function only propagates the error and does nothing else: B1's SHEET-MARK-E6/N1 ("produce no MarksProduced at all"), B2's N1 (explicitly: "offline carry-forward is the caller's/runtime's responsibility, out of this function's contract"), B3's closing clause ("shall never emit an empty or all-degraded marks set in its place"). Both directions land on the same seam: the EARS states one offline behavior as if it belongs here; the code visibly splits it across a crate boundary this audit cannot see or verify.

The code+tests pin a much richer taxonomy under "degraded symbol mark" than SHEET-MARK-005's two-clause text states, unanimously reconstructed by B1/B2/B3: three distinct `DegradeReason` variants (`SubCent` for a positive price rounding to ≤0 cents or an exact 0.0/negative reading, `Permanent` for a non-finite price or a terminal `#N/A`, `TimedOut` for a symbol still `Transient`/absent with no prior mark after `max_polls` — default 8 — elapses); a carry-forward rule that applies ONLY to the `TimedOut` path when a prior mark exists (Permanent never carries forward, even with a prior mark present, per `permanent_error_degrades_immediately_no_prior_carry`); the `round_half_to_even`/`SCALE = 1_000_000` price-conversion rule; and a strict mutual-exclusivity invariant (a symbol lands in exactly one of `MarksProduced.marks` or `.degraded`, never both — made explicit only in B3). None of this granularity is present in SHEET-MARK-005's literal text ("a degraded symbol mark shall feed... while offline, kernels shall use last cached marks"). This is real code-side surplus relative to the one EARS ID disclosed, though it plausibly belongs to sibling SHEET-MARK-00x specs not shown here, so its status as drift (vs. correctly out-of-scope for -005 specifically) is less certain than the BD finding above.

notes:
Not scored as a finding, but worth flagging: all three A-runs invented an explicit \"push\" feed mechanism for clause 1 (a trait/function call into ledger-core: A1's `LedgerCoreDegradation::mark_symbol_degraded`, A2's `ledger_core::mark_symbol_degraded`, A3's `PerSymbolDegradation::mark_degraded`), whereas the real code implements the feed passively — a degraded symbol is simply omitted from `to_ledger_marks()`'s output map (lib.rs L337-347), and ledger-core (per LEDGER-PNL-007, exercised indirectly via `common::replay` in `degraded_symbol_absent_from_ledger_marks_for_per_symbol_degradation`) treats the absence as the degradation signal. Per the classification rule, this is unanimous A-side invention with no textual basis for push-vs-omission (SHEET-MARK-005 only says \"shall feed,\" not how), so it is an assumption artifact, not a scored finding. Also minor: A-runs uniformly modeled \"quote-epoch stamp\" as an opaque monotonic tick (`QuoteEpoch`/u64), while the real stamp is `Date` — literally GOOGLEFINANCE's own trade date re-based to days-since-1970 (documented at L259-274) — a naming/type divergence rather than a behavioral one, so not counted as drift.

Read files: {scratch}/audit-baseline/crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs, .../src/testkit.rs, .../tests/marks.rs.
